subject: Post-call: qualification findings and path to dedicated pool (quantized)
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@oxbridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + qualifiers: dedicated (reserved) pool, isolation, SLA targets

Thanks for taking time today — good to meet the Oxbridge team. Below is a concise recap of what we heard + proposed next steps so we can align internally and move toward a POC timeline.

Top pain points you stated
- Model serving variability: 30–250ms p50 for short inference requests, but spikes and tail latency affecting throughput for batch workflows.
- Data isolation needs for IP and regulated preclinical data — you want tenant-level GPU isolation and dedicated NVMe for scratch data.
- Cost predictability during ramp: need a reservation model with a burst policy to handle weekly spikes tied to model retrain jobs.

Goals from our conversation
- Replace current multi-tenant endpoints with a reserved pool that provides predictable p50/p95 SLOs (target p95 <= 450ms for common endpoints).
- Maintain ability to run quantized model variants (8-bit) for the majority of traffic and keep FP16 burst nodes for high-fidelity experiments.
- Integrate with Oxbridge SSO and KMS for key rotation + audit logs for SOC2 evidence.

Redwood qualification notes (what we propose next)
1) Dedicated reserved pool proposal (attached term sheet): initial 8 GPUs reserved (A100/80GB class equivalent), quantization profile enabled for 70% of traffic, burst to 4 FP16 nodes during daily retrain windows.
2) Tenant isolation: isolated VPC + node-level tenancy for the reserved pool; customer-managed keys and audit log retention 13 months (can extend).
3) SLA targets: 99.5% uptime for the pool, p95 latency target 450ms for the quantized route, 250ms for FP16 short-paths (best-effort).

Immediate asks / next steps
- Sam: confirm procurement contact and timing (we discussed Nov procurement cycle).
- Oxbridge: send any SSO SAML metadata and primary KMS contact.
- Redwood: produce a short commercial term sheet + technical qualification matrix by EOD Monday.

Attachments: RDW-dedicated-capacity-term-sheet-v1.pdf (term summary), oxbridge-qualification-matrix.xlsx (technical Qs we will fill).

Thanks — I’ll loop legal/ops once you confirm procurement contact.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0122
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <sam@oxbridge.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + qualifiers: dedicated (reserved) pool, isolation, SLA targets

Appreciate the clear summary — that matches our notes. A few quick clarifications:
- The 450ms p95 target for quantized routes is acceptable as a goal; our clinical-facing endpoints will need the FP16 short-path p95 <= 300ms (we can reserve a small % of traffic for that).
- Our procurement lead is Priya Rao (procurement@oxbridge.ai) — she handles vendor terms and will want the term sheet and a simple cost run-rate estimate.
- Security: Aaron Kline (Dr. Aaron Kline) will be the security steward; he’ll want the SOC2 gap list and details on where audit logs are stored.

We’re aiming to start a 6-week POC in January, with commercial onboarding in Q2. Will that cadence work from Redwood’s side?

One small ask: can you include a recommended autoscale/burst policy for nightly retrain windows in the qualification matrix so we can see cost impact?

Thanks,
Sam
Head of ML Infrastructure, Oxbridge Therapeutics
sam@oxbridge.ai | +1 (617) 555-4456

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@oxbridge.ai>, Priya Rao <procurement@oxbridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + qualifiers: dedicated (reserved) pool, isolation, SLA targets

Thanks Sam — copying Priya and Aaron for procurement/security items. Priya, great to e-meet — attaching the RDW term sheet and a quick cost sketch for the reserved 8-GPU pool with the burst policy Sam described.

Quick answers to asks:
- POC cadence: Jan start for a 6-week POC works. We’ll propose milestones: week 1 onboarding & network connectivity, week 2 workload validation (latency & correctness), weeks 3–5 scale and stress runs with retrain bursts, week 6 ops handoff & SLO review.
- Autoscale/burst policy (high-level): baseline reserved capacity = 8 GPUs; automatic burst allocation up to 4 additional FP16 nodes when queue latency > 200ms for > 30s, with a daily hard cap and cost-guard rails. We’ll add a per-hour cost estimate in the matrix.
- Security artifacts: will share SOC2 artifact list + logging retention options.

Next steps from us by Monday EOD:
- Completed qualification matrix with latency profiles and suggested burst settings.
- Draft commercial term sheet (attached).
- Proposed kickoff agenda for the POC.

If Priya wants a separate pricing worksheet (Excel) we can produce a 3-tier run-rate (baseline, baseline+burst, baseline+burst+FP16 experiments).

Best,
Evelyn

Attachment stubs: RDW-dedicated-capacity-term-sheet-v1.pdf (see page 2 for pricing bands), oxbridge-qualification-matrix.xlsx
